Hi Asha / Devon — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a concrete short plan so we can validate model fit for your Knowledge Assistant use case (FAQs + SOP retrieval + short summarization).

Recap (1 line): You want high-precision grounding for SOP answers, p95 latency < 800ms, and predictable cost for a pilot serving ~10k queries/month.

What I recommend as the short pilot (minimal runway to decide):
- Run a 2-week RAG qualification on a 500–1k document slice (we've seen this size expose top retrieval/reranker differences).
- Evaluate 3 model variants (production throughput / cost trade-offs) + 2 retrieval configs.
- We (Redwood) will provide: prompt set (attached), bench template (attached), and a baseline reranker. Priyom will share exact model/config recs.

Immediate asks from you: confirm the sample corpus (who owns it), and grant read-only access to the sample folder (Drive link above) or upload to the shared S3. Also confirm whether PII redaction or on-prem deployment is required for pilot.

Proposed timeline (fast):
- Confirm sample + access: by 2027-04-18
- Redwood runs baseline eval: week of 2027-04-25
- Review results + align on next steps: 2027-04-27

Attachments: zenith_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (prompt & eval pairs), zenith-bench-template-20270411.csv (bench results CSV), zenith-data-sample-spec.md (data slice spec).

Next steps: please reply with the data owner and whether your security team requires private deployment for the trial. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if easier.

Thanks,

Hi Asha / Devon — quick technical answers + recommended baseline configs so you can decide what to send: 

Latency / capacity:
- For p95 < 800ms on short answers, a hosted small-to-medium model on Redwood Dedicated or a properly provisioned hosted route typically meets SLOs. For pilot, our recommended stack: 1) redwood-rev2-1.7B-quantized (good cost/latency) 2) redwood-rev2-7B-fp16 (higher quality at cost) 3) openlm-13b-q4 (alternate baseline)
- If you require strict isolation for PHI we can run the same config in Redwood Private (VPC) — that adds ~1–2 days setup for a temporary test environment.

Retrieval settings (baseline):
- Chunking: 600 tokens (we've found 500–700 gives best evidence granularity for SOPs)
- Embeddings: text-embed-redwood-2 (use for both indexing & retrieval)
- Vector DB: managed Pinecone or Redis, but we can use your S3 + Redwood-managed index for pilot to avoid infra work.
- Retriever recall target: aim for support_recall@5 >= 0.85 as an initial success metric.

Reranker recommendation:
- Baseline: cross-encoder (roberta-large, fine-tuned on our generic QA pairs) — good precision when ranked results are few.
- If you have labeled pairs, we can quickly fine-tune the reranker (2–3 days) and typically see 5–12% lift in grounding precision.

Grounding / quality metrics to track in the 2-week run:
- support_recall@5 (does the gold evidence appear in top 5): target >= 0.85
- grounding_precision (fraction of model answers supported by retrieved evidence): target >= 0.88
- hallucination_rate (fraction of answers with unsupported claims): target <= 0.05
- latency p50/p95 (for chosen model): p95 target <= 800ms for UX flow
- token cost per query (baseline) — we'll report tokens / USD with the benchmark CSV.

Prompt / eval artifacts I attached: zenith_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (30 canonical prompts across FAQ / SOP scenarios), and the bench CSV template outputs columns for model, retriever, reranker, recall@k, grounding_precision, hallucination_rate, p50/p95.

Short regression guardrails (we should flag quickly if):
- >2% absolute drop in support_recall@5 vs baseline model variant
- >3% increase in hallucination_rate

If these occur, step back to alternative reranker or increase chunk size / adjust retrieval weight. We'll include automated comparisons in the report.

If you confirm the sample and whether Redwood can host a read-only index, I'll spin up the baseline run and share a Drive folder with the run artifacts.

—Priyom
